clue.text: Prolonged shortage in Germany, facing turbulent time

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
turbulent water or weather is rough

explanation.surface: A long drought of something hits Germany during a stormy period.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rain is the classic case of a lasting lack of something needed.

clue.text: Ruckus about damaged tubs, means of disposing refuse

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so the noise word encloses the rest

parts.note: a ruckus is a loud din

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racket over some battered tubs at the rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish bin is the household container used to get rid of waste.

clue.text: Remove boat I've wrecked

indicators.note: a wrecked boat is broken up, so its letters with the other word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes away the boat they have smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a need or difficulty is to remove it in advance, to make it unnecessary.

clue.text: Information on American class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Details about an American school class.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the rank above species is a class of related organisms, a grouping or kind.

clue.text: Gunners destroyed flag carried by sailor in battle

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so the sailor's word goes round the rest

parts.note: tar is old slang for a sailor
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

indicators.note: a destroyed flag is torn apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Artillerymen wreck a flag held by a seaman during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: It was Nelson's 1805 naval victory over the French and Spanish fleets.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1805 sea fight off Cape Trafalgar, where Nelson died, is a famous naval battle.

clue.text: Samuel's eating large American pastries

indicators.note: one thing eating another takes it inside, so the possessive name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Sam is the short form of Samuel, so Samuel's gives SAM'S
OS stands for outsize, a label for large clothing

explanation.surface: Samuel tucks into some big American pies.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fried triangular savoury parcels of South Asian cooking, a kind of filled pastry.

clue.text: Bird's unusual sort, first of kind

indicators.note: an unusual version of the word is an altered one, so its letters are rearranged
first of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bird of an odd sort, the first of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall long-legged wading bird, said in folklore to deliver babies.

clue.text: French fellow and others achieve processing of gold maybe

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
et al is the Latin abbreviation meaning and others
to work a result is to achieve it, as in work wonders

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and colleagues manage to refine some gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaping precious or base metals into objects is a craft; gold is one example of the metal worked.

clue.text: Short of fare

parts.note: fare here is food, so being short of it means going hungry, not lacking a ticket price

explanation.surface: Lacking the money for a bus or taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a travel ticket price; it is food, as in good plain fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Deprived of food for a long time, so hungry to the point of suffering.

clue.text: Man clipping sheep who was really on the ball?

definitions.meaning: a farm worker who removes the wool from sheep

definitions.text: who was really on the ball?
definitions.meaning: Alan ..., the England footballer, who literally played with the ball

explanation.surface: A sheep clipper who was very alert.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a famous England and Newcastle striker; 'on the ball' usually means alert.
explanation.definitionFit: One who removes fleece, and the surname of a celebrated English centre-forward.

clue.text: Almost rescue girl that's plain

indicators.note: almost the whole word means the final letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: to rescue someone is to save them
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone nearly rescues a girl on an open grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical grassland with few trees is a wide flat stretch of open country, a plain.

clue.text: Fury of right during loss of power

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one letter goes within the longer word

parts.note: an outage is a cut in the electricity supply

explanation.surface: Someone's righteous anger erupts during a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name intense anger, the kind provoked by something shocking or unjust.

clue.text: Heads confer to find way up for fortune-hunter

parts.note: bean is old slang for a head, so heads are beans
to confer is to talk things over

explanation.surface: Leaders hold a meeting to find a path for an ambitious money-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: The fortune-hunter is Jack of the fairy tale, who climbed a giant plant to the giant's castle and its gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale Jack climbs a magic plant up to the sky, so it is his route upward to riches.

clue.text: Revolutionary merrymaking in bar

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the synonym is read backwards

parts.note: to revel is to make merry; revel as a noun is merrymaking

explanation.surface: Radical partying breaks out in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is a rigid rod used for prising, the simplest kind of lifting tool.

clue.text: 23 with a U-turn? Poor!

indicators.note: a U-turn reverses direction, so the compass letter for south becomes the one for north

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, meaning scruffy

explanation.surface: A cryptic question: what do you get if you turn round? Poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: S for south becomes N for north: going the opposite way is a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking money and the basics of life is poor, in want.

clue.text: Element my tribute dealt with

indicators.note: letters dealt with are handled and rearranged like cards dealt out

explanation.surface: An element that my tribute addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare-earth metal named after the Swedish village Ytterby, a chemical element.

clue.text: Five hundred overcome by force of artillery explosive

indicators.note: a thing overcome by another is swallowed up by it, so the numeral goes inside the phrase

parts.note: the strength of an army's big guns is its gun power
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Five hundred soldiers are overwhelmed by the might of the big guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Black powder is the oldest chemical explosive, used to fire guns and in fireworks.

clue.text: Conductor never sorted out church lines

indicators.note: something sorted out is rearranged into order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An orchestra's conductor never tidied the church's choir lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is a carrier of nerve impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron carries electrical signals through the body, so it is a conductor of impulses.

clue.text: Perhaps playboy later rued playing around

indicators.note: letters playing around are moved about freely, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A womaniser later regrets his philandering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing around' also describes what the answer does, which makes the clue nearly self-describing.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy who sleeps with someone other than his wife is one example of an unfaithful spouse.

clue.text: Affected manners after a period of success for home helps

indicators.note: after places the mannerisms word behind the other pieces

parts.note: an up is a good spell, as in ups and downs
to put on airs is to behave affectedly

explanation.surface: Pretentious behaviour follows a good run for the domestic staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Young foreigners who live with a family and help with housework and children are home helps.

clue.text: Strip off and run around hugging man

indicators.note: one thing hugging another holds it inside, so the jumbled word goes round the slang word
around here means the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Someone strips and streaks around embracing a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover is to take off the covering, as stripping off removes clothing.

clue.text: What 8 does for thrills?

definitions.meaning: Alan Shearer, the footballer of 8 down, strikes a ball with his foot
excitement sought for its own sake, as in doing something for fun

explanation.surface: What does the footballer do for excitement?
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer was an England centre-forward, the footballer meant in 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer strikes the ball with his foot, and the plural noun is slang for thrills or excitement.

clue.text: Anger over a disease

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger, from the humour of yellow bile

explanation.surface: Fury at an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute infection of the intestine spread by contaminated water, a deadly disease.

clue.text: To convince, declare hedging unexpectedly fits

indicators.note: to hedge is to fence in, so the speaking word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to declare something is to say it

indicators.note: letters behaving unexpectedly fall out of their usual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: To persuade someone, you declare something that fits by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone that a claim is true is to convince or persuade them of it.

clue.text: Summary of what was said about walker

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the summary word is written backwards

parts.note: a recap is a brief run-through of what has been said

explanation.surface: A précis of someone's comments about a hiker.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that moves at a lateral gait, or anyone setting the speed, is one that walks or paces.

clue.text: Squabble involving European, top journalist and bishop over swift craft

indicators.note: a thing involving others contains them, so the row word wraps the rest

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
ED is short for editor, the journalist in charge
B is the chess notation for bishop
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A row breaks out between a European, an editor and a bishop over a fast boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorboat built for speed is a fast vessel, a swift craft.

clue.text: Scruffy grain before start of year

parts.note: a grain is a single seed of a cereal plant

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Shabby grain sown at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby and squalid in appearance, run-down or unkempt.

clue.text: Large peer turns funny

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A big aristocrat becomes a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing in a dry, whimsical way; a quietly comic manner.

clue.text: Popular speaker's account

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion
a speaker's instrument is the voice

explanation.surface: A well-liked orator gives a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill sent for goods or services is an account to be settled.

clue.text: Running mates, English ones making big strides

parts.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides, so lopers make them

explanation.surface: English running partners take long strides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running mates' looks like a political term or a jogging pair; it means couples running away to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run off secretly to wed are mates, partners, on the run together.

clue.text: Crowd on vacation ply strong drink

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly crowd pressing together

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its contents, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in a crowd ply each other with liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the rough cider of the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough farmhouse cider from western England is notoriously potent, a strong drink.

clue.text: Calm a baby heartlessly with this?

definitions.text: Calm a baby heartlessly with this?

parts.note: to lull is to calm or soothe

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letters are removed, leaving only the outer two

explanation.surface: A question about what might soothe an infant, cruelly or otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle bedtime song is sung to soothe an infant into sleep.
